terra.problem: The text says they act at morning’s light, not that the plan is finished before coffee gets cold.
The joke mentions coffee, which is outside the permitted foods.
The text does not say that wanting someone else’s property is where the whole scheme starts.
Saying they are not growing anything goes beyond what the text says.
The text does not establish that they are not protecting anybody’s land.
Saying the proud strut is gone goes further than the LORD’s words that they will not walk so proudly.
Saying the proud walk stops goes further than the LORD’s words that they will not walk so proudly.
The lament speaks of the portion of a people, not specifically a family’s share. It also does not say the lament is sung.
The verse says the portion is removed; it does not say whether it is overgrown.
Saying they lose their say is broader than having no one to divide the land by lot for them.
The text does not say they tell others to stop preaching because they are sure disgrace cannot touch them. It also does not establish that they never ask whether the message is true.
The verse does not say whether the most powerful person gets a bigger share.
Saying power does not matter is broader than what the verse says about the LORD’s words bringing good to the one who walks uprightly.
The passage describes harm done by the people; it does not establish that they are not also being hurt.
The explanation assigns the comparison to how the people doing the stripping act. The text places it with the unsuspecting passersby.

The man falsely offers to preach about wine and strong drink; the text does not say he promises to provide them. Their supposed happiness at listening is also stated as fact rather than as Papa Dorin’s guess.
The passage does not identify the speakers in verse 6 as this particular group or specify that they address real preachers. It also does not say nobody would run the hypothetical man off.
Saying the people would be glad to have the man assigns them a feeling the text does not state.
Paying to see a camel in a pen is an unclear joke rather than a relatable or funny image.
Identifying Micah as a prophet and messenger introduces a fact from outside this passage without a reference.
